name: Dirt Roads
blurb: Masons can build a dirt road across an open border (75 wood, 25 gold). Units move 25% faster along it.

name: Wooden Walls
blurb: Masons can close an open border with a wooden palisade (150 wood, 100 gold). Both provinces must keep at least one other way in and out.

name: Building: Stable
blurb: Unlocks the Stable, which lets a Barracks in the same province train Cavalry.

name: Building: Marketplace
blurb: Unlocks the Marketplace: +3 gold every payout, buildable in any province.

name: Building: Granary
blurb: Unlocks the Granary: +1000 food storage each (the nation starts able to hold 2000).

name: Building: Storehouse
blurb: Unlocks the Storehouse: +1000 wood storage each (the nation starts able to hold 2000).

name: Building: Bank
blurb: Unlocks the Bank: +1000 gold storage each (the nation starts able to hold 2000).

name: Fort Charters I
blurb: Raises the Fort limit from 3 to 5.

name: Automating Wayfinders
blurb: Idle Wayfinders survey explored, unsurveyed provinces on their own. Toggle it on a Wayfinder’s command card.

name: Arrowslits
blurb: Forts and capitals slowly shoot at enemy armies standing in their province, wearing them down while they try to capture it.

name: Advanced Farms
blurb: Every Farm gives +1 food.

name: Advanced Lumber Mills
blurb: Every Lumber Mill gives +1 wood.

name: Advanced Gold Mines
blurb: Every Gold Mine gives +2 gold.

name: Building: Mage Tower
blurb: Unlocks the Mage Tower, which trains Mages and opens Magic research. Your first tower lets you choose a school of magic.

name: Gravel Roads
blurb: Every road is relaid in gravel: units move 35% faster along roads.

name: Stone Walls
blurb: Walls are built of stone, and existing palisades are rebuilt in stone: three times as strong.

name: Fort Charters II
blurb: Raises the Fort limit from 5 to 7.

name: Wayfinder Stealth
blurb: Wayfinders can sneak: three times slower, but enemy armies can’t see them. Without it, an enemy army that finds a Wayfinder kills him.

name: Refined Farms
blurb: Every Farm gives another +1 food.

name: Refined Lumber Mills
blurb: Every Lumber Mill gives another +1 wood.

name: Refined Gold Mines
blurb: Every Gold Mine gives another +2 gold.

name: Cobblestone Roads
blurb: Every road is paved with cobbles: units move 50% faster along roads.

name: Wall Gates
blurb: Masons can build a gate into a wall between two of your provinces. Only your units can pass; enemies must break the wall.

name: Fort Charters III
blurb: Raises the Fort limit from 7 to 9.

name: Far-Seeing Wayfinders
blurb: Wayfinders see into every province next to the one they stand in.

name: Sophisticated Farms
blurb: Every Farm gives another +1 food.

name: Sophisticated Lumber Mills
blurb: Every Lumber Mill gives another +1 wood.

name: Sophisticated Gold Mines
blurb: Every Gold Mine gives another +2 gold.

name: Pikes
blurb: Pike for the Armory: attack 7, two-handed. +50% damage against cavalry.

name: Bastard Swords
blurb: Bastard Sword for the Armory: attack 8, one-handed. Parry: take 10% less damage.

name: Maces
blurb: Mace for the Armory: attack 7, two-handed. Crushing: ignores half of enemy armor.

name: Round Shields
blurb: Round Shield for one-handed designs: +2 armor.

name: Leather II Armor
blurb: Leather II armor for the Armory: 2 armor, +10% speed.

name: Chain I Armor
blurb: Chain I armor for the Armory: 3 armor, no speed change.

name: Horse Breeding
blurb: Cavalry can ride Arabians (fastest, fragile) or Mongolian horses (cheap to feed, at home in forest and swamp, weak charge).

name: Polearms
blurb: Polearm for the Armory: attack 9, two-handed. +50% damage against cavalry.

name: Long Swords
blurb: Long Sword for the Armory: attack 10, one-handed. Parry: take 10% less damage.

name: Morning Stars
blurb: Morning Star for the Armory: attack 9, two-handed. Crushing: ignores half of enemy armor.

name: Kite Shields
blurb: Kite Shield for one-handed designs: +4 armor.

name: Leather III Armor
blurb: Leather III armor for the Armory: 3 armor, +10% speed.

name: Chain II Armor
blurb: Chain II armor for the Armory: 5 armor, no speed change.

name: Plate I Armor
blurb: Plate I armor for the Armory: 6 armor, −15% speed.

name: Plate II Armor
blurb: Plate II armor for the Armory: 9 armor, −15% speed.

name: Horse Training
blurb: Unlocks Friesians (the hardest charge) and armored Percherons (toughest, but slow and hungry).

name: Halberds
blurb: Halberd for the Armory: attack 12, two-handed. +50% damage against cavalry.

name: Great Swords
blurb: Great Sword for the Armory: attack 14, two-handed. Parry: take 10% less damage.

name: War Hammers
blurb: War Hammer for the Armory: attack 12, two-handed. Crushing: ignores half of enemy armor.

name: Tower Shields
blurb: Tower Shield for one-handed designs: +7 armor, but 8% slower.

name: Aegiss
blurb: Aegis for one-handed designs: +10 armor.

name: Leather IV Armor
blurb: Leather IV armor for the Armory: 4 armor, +10% speed.

name: Chain III Armor
blurb: Chain III armor for the Armory: 7 armor, no speed change.

name: Chain IV Armor
blurb: Chain IV armor for the Armory: 9 armor, no speed change.

name: Plate III Armor
blurb: Plate III armor for the Armory: 12 armor, −15% speed.

name: Plate IV Armor
blurb: Plate IV armor for the Armory: 15 armor, −15% speed.

name: School of Life
blurb: Commit to Life magic: harvests, protective skins, healing and the forest.

name: School of Death
blurb: Commit to Death magic: cursed weapons, mountain passages, the risen dead and grave riches.

name: School of the Arcane
blurb: Commit to Arcane magic: far sight from towers, mind reading, trading across worlds, traps and rifts.

name: Harvest
blurb: Mages can cast Harvest: +10% food from all Farms while the Mage keeps casting, up to 3 minutes. 6-minute nationwide cooldown.

name: Bountiful Harvest
blurb: Harvest gives +20% farm food and 200 food when cast. Cooldown drops to 4 minutes.

name: Magnificent Harvest
blurb: Harvest gives +30% farm food for as long as the Mage casts, and 400 food for every full 3 minutes of casting. No cooldown.

name: Hardened Skin
blurb: Autocast: when an army with a Mage starts a battle, its soldiers get +5% health. 5-minute cooldown per army.

name: Stone Skin
blurb: Skin spell gives +10% health; cooldown 3 minutes.

name: Diamond Skin
blurb: Skin spell gives +15% health; cooldown 90 seconds.

name: Mending
blurb: Mages heal an army’s wounds back to full over 1 minute. 3-minute cooldown.

name: Rejuvenation
blurb: Healing takes 30 seconds; cooldown 2 minutes.

name: Restoration
blurb: Healing is instant and has no cooldown.

name: Speak with the Forest
blurb: A Mage can open a path through a border of trees after 2 minutes of casting. Lumber Mills are unaffected.

name: Commune with Nature
blurb: Opening a forest path takes 1 minute.

name: Arboreal Restoration
blurb: A Mage can close a forest path again with 1 minute of casting.

name: Cursed Weapons I
blurb: Autocast: when an army with a Mage starts a battle, its weapons deal +5% damage. 5-minute cooldown per army.

name: Cursed Weapons II
blurb: Cursed Weapons deal +10% damage; cooldown 3 minutes.

name: Cursed Weapons III
blurb: Cursed Weapons deal +15% damage; cooldown 90 seconds.

name: Underworld Passage
blurb: A Mage can open a tunnel through a mountain border after 2 minutes of casting.

name: Hallways of Pain
blurb: Opening a mountain tunnel takes 1 minute.

name: Sealed Gates
blurb: A Mage can seal a mountain tunnel again with 1 minute of casting.

name: Risen Dead
blurb: Autocast: an army with a Mage that isn’t using Cursed Weapons raises 1 fallen soldier every 15 seconds in battle. 2-minute cooldown after the battle.

name: Necromantic Energies
blurb: Raises 2 fallen soldiers every 15 seconds.

name: Army of Death
blurb: Raises 3 fallen soldiers every 15 seconds.

name: Grave Robbing
blurb: A 5-minute cast that yields 500 gold.

name: Death Taxes
blurb: The 5-minute cast yields 1000 gold.

name: Charon’s Riches
blurb: The 5-minute cast yields 2000 gold.

name: Arcane Scouts
blurb: Every Mage Tower (and its upgrades) sees all neighboring provinces, permanently.

name: Arcane Vision
blurb: Mage Towers reveal stealthed units within their sight.

name: Clear Thoughts
blurb: While a Mage casts, every army within 3 provinces of him is revealed. No cooldown.

name: Mind Reading
blurb: While a Mage casts, every army on the map is revealed. No cooldown.

name: Interdimensional Trading
blurb: A 2-minute cast that yields 100 food, 100 gold and 100 wood.

name: Interdimensional Stockmarket
blurb: The 2-minute cast yields 200 of each resource.

name: Stasis Trap
blurb: A Mage sets a trap in his province; the next enemy army there can’t leave for 10 seconds (it can still fight). One trap at a time; 1-minute cooldown after it springs.

name: Stasis Prison
blurb: The trap holds for 20 seconds.

name: Teleportation Rift
blurb: A Mage opens a rift where he stands. Later, a casting Mage anywhere can send one army through it to the rift. Single use.

name: Teleportation Portal
blurb: Rifts can be used 3 times.

name: Grand Staves
blurb: Mages can carry a Grand Stave: attack 6 (Stave 4).

name: Mythic Staves
blurb: Mages can carry a Mythic Stave: attack 9.

name: Cryptic Wands
blurb: Mages can carry a Cryptic Wand: attack 3 (Wand 2), leaving a hand free for a shield.

name: Enigmatic Wands
blurb: Mages can carry an Enigmatic Wand: attack 5, with a shield.

name: Abandon Magic School
blurb: Costs 1000 gold to begin. When finished, your school and all of its spells are forgotten, and you can choose a new school.
